boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Fort Bisland record (April 12-13, 1863) in Operations in West Louisiana [April 1863]. Grover's landing at Indian Bend on April 13 and Irish Bend on April 14 belong to LA007. Campaign-wide movements (the Berwick Bay crossing of April 9-11, the pursuit to Opelousas and Alexandria) and multi-day loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Banks's Department of the Gulf, XIX Army Corps [US] and District of Western Louisiana [CS]; the live field reads zero. Irwin says Banks had 10,000 men while Taylor reports 4,000 men with four batteries, estimated at 24 or 25 guns; he says Banks set out with seven brigades and fifty-six guns for the whole campaign. Taylor says at least 14,000 men and about sixty guns were displayed in his front on April 13 against his army of less than 4,000 at the start.
claims.rationale: Figures from a history and an interested report; the Union figures differ, and Grover's division, detached to the lake, is inside the campaign total. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

Taylor says his right rested on a swamp and his left on woods ending in a swamp.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory and the live result Union Victory. Taylor says the enemy had gained no ground by the close of April 13 and that he evacuated because of the landing in his rear; Irwin and NPS say the Union skirmishers found the works abandoned the next morning.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The position was given up for the turning movement, not taken by assault.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Total 684 (US 234; CS 450); the live field reads 674 total (US 224; CS 450). Irwin gives the corps' loss as 3 officers and 37 men killed and 8 officers and 176 men wounded (224), and says the Confederate losses were never reported. Taylor says he could not yet estimate his loss; the Diana lost 2 killed and 5 wounded.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Irwin's 224 matches the live Union figure, not the frozen 234.

open_questions: Banks's No. 1 report and return of casualties, Weitzel's, Emory's, Arnold's and the other Union reports (Nos. 2-23), Kirby Smith's No. 38 and Mouton's No. 40 reports, Sibley's account and the naval reports remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Richard B. Irwin's History of the Nineteenth Army Corps (Putnam's, 1892), already registered for the Red River pass, is an interested Union history by the corps' later assistant adjutant-general. Its Teche chapters cite Taylor's report and the nominal lists, so it is not independent of them. Taylor's April 23, 1863 report (Official Records Series I, Volume XV, a shared container) is an interested Confederate account; it is placed in the group of his 1864 Red River reports as one author family. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
